question: At a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, what advance placement distance does Table 2C-3 show for deceleration to an advisory speed of 30 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, Table 2C-3 shows an advance placement distance of 275 feet for Condition B deceleration to a 30 mph advisory speed. This distance is based on a 2.5-second PRT, a deceleration rate of 10 feet/second², and is adjusted for a 250-foot sign legibility distance. Guidance (recommended): - Warning signs should be placed so that they provide an adequate PRT; per Section 2C.04, "The distances contained in Table 2C-3 should be applied with engineering judgment," and "The effectiveness of the placement of warning signs should be periodically evaluated under both day and night conditions." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-3 shows the 60 mph row intersecting the Condition B "30" advisory-speed column at 275 ft. - [Image 3] Page 152 presents Section 2C.04 and Table 2C-3, confirming the 60 mph / 30 mph cell value of 275 ft along with table footnote 4 explaining the Condition B deceleration basis (2.5-second PRT, 10 feet/second² deceleration, 250-foot legibility distance). Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152)
